repo_notes.content: vidbyte-memory is a GitHub template, not a library: users click 'Use this template', replace the '## Task' block in AGENTS.md with one recurring task, and let their coding agent work in the repo. The core idea is correction-driven memory: every human correction is logged verbatim and handed to three subagents (fact, test, update), which turn it into slim facts or rules in facts/ and memory/, deterministic pytest tests in tests/ or verifier agents in verifiers/, and updates to older memory. scripts/footprint.py ends every request with a commit whose message is the memory delta. Document the protocol and the reasons behind it (memory files are never rewritten whole; memory is context while tests and the Stop hook are enforcement; facts are admitted only through five checks). Ignore .github/assets and docs/design.

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: What the template is, who it is for, the correction-driven memory loop from request to footprint commit, and what it is not (no database, no service, one owner and one task per repo).

pages.title: Starting a task repo
pages.purpose: Creating a repo from the template, filling the Task block in AGENTS.md, the first test run, and which template-only files to delete.

pages.title: The AGENTS.md runtime protocol
pages.purpose: The start-of-request, generation, feedback, pausing and end-of-request steps in AGENTS.md, the stopping condition, and the checklist an agent must satisfy.

pages.title: Memory types and entry format
pages.purpose: memory/MAP.md: each typed memory file, entry ids and metadata lines, statuses (active, superseded, retired) and the write rule for each file.

pages.title: Facts and admission checks
pages.purpose: facts/ and skills/create-fact/SKILL.md: the five admission checks, the 4-to-5-sentence fact format, and routing between facts, rules and hints.

pages.title: Feedback handling and the three subagents
pages.purpose: skills/handle-feedback/SKILL.md and prompts/: logging feedback verbatim, the fact, test and update subagents with disjoint write scopes, stitching, and dispositions.

pages.title: Tests, verifiers and verification rounds
pages.purpose: tests/ (including test_memory_integrity.py), verifiers/ and skills/verify-generation/SKILL.md: how feedback becomes a deterministic test or a verifier agent, and the 3-to-5-round stopping condition.

pages.title: Footprint commits and the Stop hook
pages.purpose: scripts/footprint.py (counts, delta, commit message, Memory-Template trailer, --no-marker) and scripts/guard.py (the Claude Code Stop hook and its five-round cap).

pages.title: Harness support
pages.purpose: How the template runs in Claude Code (subagent wrappers in .claude/agents, Stop hook in .claude/settings.json) versus Codex, Cursor and other AGENTS.md harnesses, where the protocol is followed by hand.

pages.title: Contributing and releases
pages.purpose: The contribution rules in .github/CONTRIBUTING.md, CI workflows in .github/workflows, CHANGELOG.md and how releases credit requesters.
